plans.premise: The user provides the exchange: “Did you finish the poster?” “Not quite.”
plans.mechanism: Over four short exchanges, explain that the reply indicates incomplete work without specifying how much remains; discuss how it differs from “not yet,” then apply the distinction to the user’s new sentence about a draft. The user supplies both texts in the dialogue.
plans.diversity_key: partial completion versus timing in a conversational reply

plans.premise: The user supplies two versions of a note: “I packed the cups, plates and napkins.” and “I packed the cups, plates, and napkins.”
plans.mechanism: Over four short exchanges, explain that the final comma is an optional serial comma in this simple list and does not change the intended items; discuss consistency, then punctuate a different list supplied by the user without adding items.
plans.diversity_key: optional serial comma and list punctuation

plans.premise: The user shares a fictional message: “Thanks for checking. The blue cover looks good to me. I haven’t seen the green one.”

plans.diversity_key: expressed approval versus absence of evaluation

plans.premise: The user provides a short exchange: “The hall is ready.” “Then we can start.”
plans.mechanism: Over four short exchanges, explain how “then” links the second statement to the first as a consequence in this context, while noting it can also mark sequence elsewhere; discuss the user’s contrasting sentence “We ate, then left,” and apply the intended link to a further user-supplied line.
